title: Operational decision canvas for launch probes
content:
Purpose: quick operational decision canvas to run traffic probes (smoke/ramp/soak/chaos) for major launches. This is a working note — not final. Use as a single source for launch day decisions and rapid triage.

Context and scope:
- Applies to feature launches that change model routes, traffic split, or introduce new routing/fallback policies (hosted + dedicated).
- Not for low-risk UI copy changes. Use when expected traffic > 5k reqs/day or when model variant changes are non-trivial.
- Audience: product-ops, infra, SRE, PM, solutions eng.

Quick TL;DR (one-line): run a 3-phase probe (smoke -> ramp -> soak) with clear KPI gates (latency p50/p95, p99; error rate; unit cost; model quality signal) and explicit rollback actions owned by eng oncall + PM.

Probe taxonomy (what we mean by probe types):
- Smoke: <1% traffic, short (10–30m). Verify basic connectivity, auth, and major error floors.
- Ramp: staged increase (1% -> 10% -> 25%) over hours. Checks throughput/backpressure and scaling.
- Soak: sustained load at target percentage for 24–72h to catch memory leaks, slow drift.
- Chaos (optional): simulated node loss or regional failover while ramp/soak running. Only when doing infra resilience tests and with SRE signoff.

KPI watchlist (primary signals):
- Latency: p50, p95, p99 (tokens out) — baseline and delta. Example gates: p95 delta > +30% -> alert, p99 delta > +50% -> block.
- Error rate: 5xx or 429s per minute. Gate: sustained >0.5% for 15m -> escalate.
- Model quality regression: sampled prompts -> human eval or automated eval score. Gate: >3pt drop vs baseline on critical prompt set -> block.
- Unit cost: $/1k tokens; watch for >20% increase vs baseline (investigate quantization/route mistakes).
- Token throughput and queue depth: continuous. Queue depth > threshold -> reduce canary.
- Customer-facing errors: number of unique customer errors (high weight).

Decision matrix (simple):
- Green (all gates within thresholds): proceed to next percentage step. Owner: product-ops leading, engineering keeps watch.
- Yellow (one non-critical signal): hold for stabilization window (15–60m depending on metric). Owner: eng lead to triage; product ops pauses ramp.
- Red (critical signal per gate): rollback to previous stable model/route immediately. Owner: oncall SRE + PM (execute rollback playbook).

Owners & roles (prelaunch):
- Product Ops (Maya): runbook steward, coordinates probes and comms.
- PM (Jordan): business decision maker — approves go/no-go at each phase.
- Eng infra lead (Priya): executes routing changes, monitors infra metrics.
- SRE oncall (rotation): executes rollback, postmortem owner if incident.
- Solutions Eng (Evan): customer impact triage.

Run schedule example (fast path):
- T+0: Smoke (1%) — 30m watch — pass ->
- T+1h: Ramp to 10% — 1h watch -> pass ->
- T+3h: Ramp to 25% — 2h watch -> pass ->
- T+6h: Soak at 50% or target for 24h (depending on launch).
Notes: adjust cadence for regional launches or heavy model weight.

Rollback checklist (short):
1) Notify #launch-control Slack with rollback intent and reason.
2) Route traffic back to pinned stable variant (tagged in routing config).
3) Disable new config/feature flags.
4) Confirm error rate/latency returning to baseline.
5) Open JIRA incident: OPS-xxxxx, tag for postmortem.
6) Communicate to stakeholders + customers per comms plan.

Stabilization heuristics (how long to hold):
- Latency spike: 30–60m stabilization window (sticky).
- Error bursts: if >1% sustained for 15m -> rollback.
- Model quality drift (automated sample): require human check; if confirmed, block further ramps.

Checklist for probe kickoff (pre-lift):
- [ ] Confirm stable baseline metrics (last 7 days) attached to ticket.
- [ ] All owners invited to stand-by channel (#launch-control).
- [ ] Routing plan pushed to infra repo and reviewed: github:inference/rollouts#238.
- [ ] Canary percentage schedule documented in ticket.
- [ ] Alerting thresholds set in Prometheus/Datadog; test alerts fired once.
- [ ] Recovery playbook ready and smoke-tested (who executes, how long to revert).
- [ ] QA sample set & auto-eval harness pointed at canary route.

Sprint tracker snippet (working table):
- Week 1: prep baseline data, define probe plan, set alerts. Owners: Maya / Priya.
- Week 2: dry-run smoke, test rolling config, finalize comms. Owners: Eng + Product.
- Week 3: staged launch + soak, post-launch triage.

Open questions / TODOs:
- Finalize automated quality threshold for the sampled prompt set (mechanics + owner). TODO @Evan.
- Confirm cost alerting hook for sudden egress/ops costs. TODO @Finance liaison.
- Should we gate canary by customer tier? (enterprise-only first). Follow up with sales.

Post-launch artifacts (what to produce):
- Short incident timeline (if any) and key metrics snapshot at time of event.
- Postmortem within 5 business days if rollback or sustained degradation.
- Optimization log: decisions made to reduce cost/latency and their impact.

Notes to self: this canvas is intentionally compact — aim for one-page decision brief on launch day. Keep references to longer playbooks but avoid duplicating steps.

References and quick links:
- Confluence: PRODOPS-Launch-Canary-Playbook
- Jira: OPS-7123 (canary automation), PROD-4012 (routing policy change)
- GitHub PR: inference/rollouts#238 (routing config)

Recent changes (changelog):
- 2025-11-02: created initial canvas (Maya).
- 2025-11-12: added soak guidance and cost gates (Priya).
- 2025-11-19: updated owners and added sample sprint tracker (Maya).

If you’re on this doc: add short bullet edits, no long essays. We will convert final to a one-page PDF for launch brief.
